subject: Re: Observability & Evals — scope, win criteria, next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Berg <sofia.berg@finopsco.com>
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finopsco.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Observability & Evals — quick recap and next steps

Sofia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side to lock scope and success criteria so we can size an eval that demonstrates wins for FinOpsCo. TL;DR: you want token-level observability + fast regression detection tied to golden prompts, plus a low-friction eval that validates cost/latency tradeoffs.

Pain points we captured:
- No token-level tracing: you can see overall latency & error rates in Datadog, but not per-prompt/token breakdowns (makes debugging hallucinations/timeouts slow).
- Regression detection: golden prompt set exists, but it’s a manual run and there’s no automated alerting when outputs degrade.
- Dashboards are scattershot: teams build ad-hoc views, want a standardized SLO dashboard for model quality + cost.
- Deployment guardrails: worried about a rollout accidentally increasing token spend or degrading output quality.

Success criteria you mentioned (confirm if I missed anything):
- 95th pctl latency for common chat flows < 300ms at your baseline traffic (approx 1k qps burst).
- Regression alerting: detect quality regressions on golden prompts within 1 hour and create automatic triage tickets.
- Token cost visibility: per-route token breakdown and monthly forecasting that ties back to product features.
- Safe rollout: ability to canary model/quantization changes and auto-fallback to a previous variant on quality regression.

Current stack notes you shared: k8s-hosted LLM inference (Llama2-13B quantized), Datadog for infra metrics, and an internal prompt library.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll share a short eval playbook (attached) with the scope and checklist.
2) Technical follow-up: Dev will send a tiny tracing snippet you can drop into your inference layer to validate traces against our collector.
3) Schedule a 90-min kickoff for an in-context eval (we recommend the week of July 11).
4) We’ll prepare an SLO dashboard mock and a golden-prompt harness you can run against a sandbox.

Attachments: redwood-eval-playbook.xlsx (playbook + checklist)

If the items above look right, can you confirm availability for a kickoff the week of July 11 and whether your infra team can provision a short-lived sandbox or API key?

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast on this.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
cal: https://calendly.com/jasmine-redwood/30m | +1 (415) 555-0127
From: Sofia Berg <sofia.berg@finopsco.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2027 13:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Observability & Evals — quick recap and next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — this is great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tech stack: we run Llama2-13B quantized in-house on k8s (NVIDIA A10G), traffic goes through an internal API gateway. Datadog receives host/infra metrics; we do not currently ingest token-level traces.
- Golden prompts: we have a set of ~120 prompts used by Product & Trust; they’re maintained in a private repo and are run ad-hoc (~monthly). We’d like these automated and integrated into CI if possible.
- Cost target: we need to see an expected unit cost reduction (tokens/$) or clear levers (batching/kv cache suggestions) before we commit to a broader rollout.
- Stakeholders: Oliver Chen (CTO) and Priya (Head of Product — she’s OOO until 7/6 but will join the kickoff if timing works).

For the sandbox: we can spin up a short-lived namespace and a service account token for the week of July 11. I’ll confirm exact windows next week.

Would love to see the SLO dashboard mock and the tracing snippet — Oliver is specifically interested in examples of multi-tenant tracing that tie tokens to user sessions.

Best,
Sofia
VP, Engineering — FinOpsCo
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Berg <sofia.berg@finopsco.com>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finopsco.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 05:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Observability & Evals — quick recap and next steps

Folks — forwarding Sofia's confirmation. Can you help with three things before the kickoff?

1) Tracing snippet: a minimal example that instruments token-level traces and correlates them to an incoming request ID (Sofia wants an example that’s lightweight and safe to run in their k8s namespace).
2) SLO dashboard mock: screenshot/mock (not production dashboards) showing latency percentiles, token cost per route, and a golden-prompt regression panel.
3) Canary plan: short write-up of how we would run a canary (traffic split, regression threshold, automatic rollback criteria).

Attachments: redwood-eval-playbook.xlsx (from earlier)

Sofia & Oliver — we’ll loop back with the tech artifacts by EOD Friday (we'll surface any blockers).

Thanks — J
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Berg <sofia.berg@finopsco.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@finopsco.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Observability & Evals — artifacts and next steps

Sofia — quick tech note and proposed plan from engineering. Leaving Sean on the thread for the SLO/dashboard ownership.

What we’re attaching/doing now:
- tracing-snippet.patch: a tiny middleware (Python/Flask) that emits token-level spans to our collector; it tags spans with request_id and user_id. Drop-in should run in <=10ms overhead on A10G.
- slo-dashboard-mock.png: a 3-panel mock (latency pctl, per-route token spend, golden-prompt regression time-series).
- redwood-eval-playbook.xlsx: updated with a short checklist for sandbox creds and test dataset ingestion.

Proposed engineering plan (90-day quick eval cadence):
1) Kickoff (90 mins) — align scope, install snippet in sandbox, and smoke-run golden prompts. (Week of Jul 11 — we can do Tue/Wed)
2) 48-72 hour run — collect traces + eval harness results. We’ll run your 120 golden prompts and surface any regressions via an automated job that writes to your Jira project.
3) Canary & rollout guide — we’ll provide a sample canary config: start 5% traffic, run golden-prompt checks every 30 mins, rollback if regression rate > 2% or if 95p latency increases by > 20%.

Questions for you:
- Can you provide a short-lived service account/YAML and the API gateway host for the sandbox?
- Do you want the regression alerts opened as Jira tickets or Slack alerts to #ops?

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EvalPlaybook (playbook + artifacts).

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff and assign owners for the artifacts.

—
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
Attachments: tracing-snippet.patch, slo-dashboard-mock.png, redwood-eval-playbook.xlsx
